findings.summary: The second Coppertop clone ended in whiteout after 31 verified actions.

resolution.observed: The turn-001 fixed-damage replay selected Spark and the turn-008 status-fallback replay rejected burned Lildozer; both corrected actions executed with no discrepancy. The invalid bundle will not be retried.

findings.summary: Turn 1 abandoned the proven Spark opening and switched healthy Bushtank into Bibarel because the scorer doubled fixed Super Fang damage as if it were an ordinary critical-hit roll.

resolution.observed: Turn-001 replay reported a 26-damage Super Fang critical bound, selected Spark, and executed Spark with no discrepancy.

findings.why_bad: Super Fang is fixed half-current-HP damage; applying the ordinary critical multiplier created a false catastrophic threat and broke the opening policy.
findings.improvement: Use the fixed-damage exception in critical bounds and preserve the verified two-Spark Bibarel line.

findings.summary: The false opening threat produced 22 switches in 31 actions and only 9 attacks; the policy repeatedly spent enemy turns without improving the board.

resolution.observed: Turn-008 replay vetoed the burned Lildozer voluntary switch and selected healthy Ohmnomnom instead; the action executed with no discrepancy.

findings.improvement: Do not pivot from a healthy active line when the corrected fixed-damage threat is survivable; preserve the action economy for verified attacks.

findings.summary: This attempt cannot validate Coppertop as a team answer because the invalid fixed-damage threat corrupted the entire opening before the matchup plan began.

resolution.observed: The preparation finding was invalidated as a scorer-corrupted attempt: corrected turn-001 and turn-008 replays reached legal battle decisions without observation or execution discrepancies. A fresh full clone is required before judging Coppertop.

findings.improvement: Re-evaluate the prepared team only after a corrected opening reaches Ponyta and Eelektrik.

findings.summary: 22 switches consumed the line and left Coppertop at 13 HP for the final Eelektrik entry; the tempo loss was avoidable.
The fight again reached 31 verified actions; speed remains secondary to repairing the opening survival model.

correct_choices: Every action result and the terminal whiteout were RAM-verified with no tooling discrepancy.
The few attacks that occurred were legal and their PP changes were verified.
Coppertop's Bulldoze into Ponyta at turn 25 was a correct matchup action, but it occurred after the line was already unrecoverable.
